title: Hosted Endpoint Acceptance (Lite): PRD + Launch Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a compact PRD and operational playbook for a minimal-hosted endpoint bundle (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) aimed at fast go-to-market for low-to-medium traffic customers. This ticket prescribes acceptance criteria, minimal evals, rollout canary slices, and the launch checklist for the 'lite' bundle. The intent is to ship predictable behavior and a clear degradation path while deferring advanced features (fine-grained lane shaping, long-term telemetry retention) to subsequent waves.

Audience: PMs, Eng (runtime & infra), DX/SDK, Design, SRE, Security.

Success metric (G0): Launch lite bundle with deterministic behavioral contract on 95% of seeded prompts, <100ms median inference overhead versus baseline model config for curated microbenchmarks, and response-level telemetry emitted for rollout monitoring.

Notes: This PRD purposefully limits scope relative to the full hosted surface to reduce launch friction: fixed set of model variants (quantized + fp16), no tenant-specific autoscaling at GA, and single-region initial rollouts. We aim for quick operationalization and to capture learning for the full bundle launch.
scope_in_scope:
- Host endpoints for: chat (stateless conversational API), completions (prompt -> completion), embeddings (vectorize up to 2048 tokens), rerank (similarity-based reranking pipeline).
- Minimal behavioral spec per surface with ~30 seeded prompts for eval gating.
- Streaming support for chat/completions.
- Structured output hook for rerank (score + metadata).
- Canary rollout with 1% tenant and traffic slice, automated rollback triggers.
- Basic cost telemetry and per-token breakdown in Console for launched tenants.
scope_out_of_scope:
- Multi-region active-active rollout (deferred).
- Full tenant-specific autoscaling policies and burst capacity contracts.
- Advanced eval harness (extensive corpus) — only a curated seed set for acceptance.
- On-prem / VPC private deployment packaging in this ticket.
- Experimental quantization variants beyond the chosen GA configurations.
decisions: GA model set limited to two size variants per surface (default + low-cost quantized) to simplify routing and perf guarantees.
Deterministic seed behavior will be provided only for the completions surface via a seed param; chat determinism deferred due to conversation state complexity.
Canary rollout will be time-boxed (72h) with automated SLO checks; manual escalation after the window if instability observed.
No per-tenant burst SLA at GA; provide documented mitigation guidance and ticket template for customers requesting reserved capacity.
Structured output for rerank exposed as JSON with a mandatory score field and optional metadata object (flat schema) to keep client parsing simple.
tradeoffs: Narrow model set reduces complexity for rollouts but limits immediate workload-opportunity coverage for edge cases.
Using curated seed prompts accelerates launch but increases the risk of blind spots in production quality; mitigate with fast follow-up eval cycles post-GA.
Delaying per-tenant autoscaling simplifies ops but increases potential latency spikes under tenant burst — mitigated by conservative throttling and clear docs.
Enabling streaming for GA increases runtime orchestration complexity but is high-impact for developer experience; selected for chat/completions only.
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral: For each surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) the curated seed set must pass acceptance thresholds: mean pass rate >= 95% across functional probes defined in the acceptance doc.

Performance: End-to-end p95 latency for the GA model configuration measured on internal traffic simulations must be within configured lane SLOs (chat p95 < 300ms for single-turn prompts, completions p95 < 400ms for 512-token generation scenario).
Cost: Per-token cost telemetry present in Console and matches runtime billing signals within 5% for sampled requests.
Reliability: Canary slice (1% traffic, up to 10 tenants) must maintain request success rate >= 99.5% over 72 hours; automated rollback triggers if below 99%.
Observability: Trace-level sampling and per-request metadata (model_version, quantization_profile, route_lanes, cost_estimate) emitted to telemetry backend and visible on the launch dashboard.
Security: API keys and KMS integration tested for hosted-surface calls; no plaintext model artifacts exposed in logs. Security sign-off required prior to scheduled GA cut.
SDK/Docs: Quickstart snippets for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank are published and validated in the developer experience harness (smoke tests pass).
Compatibility: Function-calling surface and streaming responses verified with our SDKs (Node/Python) against the GA endpoint contracts.

Prepare Console cost & latency dashboard widgets for launch (Product + DX).
Security review and penetration checklist completion (Security).
Write SDK quickstart examples and run smoke tests (DX/SDK).
Author customer-facing launch notes and mitigation guide for burst behavior (PM + Support).
Run cross-team launch readiness review and record decision log (All teams).
